quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Only use your mirrors to see all around you.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to pass other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These signs tell drivers the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: How can you help drivers merging from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Move to another lane if you can.
Do not worry about it because they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them plenty of space to merge safely by moving to a different lane if possible.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark. Slow down and increase your following distance when riding at night. Use your high beam anytime you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about a motorcycle with a sidecar?

options.text: It can tip over if turning too fast.
It can take any corner at any speed.
It should not be used to carry items.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can tip over if turning too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast for the corner.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider extends their left arm straight out?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of turn signals to show their intentions. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do when it starts raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane in wet conditions. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead. The left tire track is often the best option, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to make yourself more visible.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which body part operates the gearshift lever?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: Which is NOT a requirement for an effective eye or face shield?
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, resistant to penetration, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. It should not be airtight.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do about space cushions?
questions.explanation: Ride close together as a group, but always keep enough space around each rider to stay safe.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help reduce crash risk?
questions.explanation: Be visible and use clear signals. Watch for hazards and stay ready to react. Do not rely on hoping other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which item does NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots, and gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection.

questions.question: Which item is NOT considered protective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear a leather jacket, heavy denim pants, and full-fingered gloves. Wear lace-up boots or high-top boots, not athletic shoes.

questions.question: Which is NOT a risk of riding in cold weather for long periods?
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause fatigue, hypothermia, and severe chills. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself.

questions.question: After entering a turn, what should you do with the throttle?

options.text: Keep steady speed or accelerate slowly

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep steady speed or accelerate slowly
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle smoothly through the turn. Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually. This keeps your motorcycle stable.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects your face in a crash
Does not work as well as goggles
Should not be used with a helmet

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your face in a crash
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face during a crash. It also shields you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks while riding.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to reduce speed. Lean forward and down, and get off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of for the best protection?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material to protect your hands properly.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle sits lower with a passenger's weight. Ride slower than usual, especially on curves and bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep a larger space cushion when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: As you slow down or stop, what should you do with the gears?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is only a personal choice.
Yes, but only if clothing is loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good clothing can reduce injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Choose sturdy material that fits snug so it does not flap in the wind.
